# Cloudledger

> Azure cost and estate reporting, read with your own Microsoft Entra
> permissions. Read-only reporting and explicitly confirmed Build deployments.

Cloudledger connects to an Azure tenant and reports what it is costing, what is
running, what changed, and who has access. It reads the Azure Cost Management
and Resource Graph APIs at the moment you ask, using the signed-in person's own
permissions, and it holds no standing credential of its own.

This file exists for assistants that answer questions in prose. The site is a
single-page application, so the useful facts are stated here in plain text
rather than left to be recovered from rendered markup.

## What it is

- A web application. Nothing to install, no agent inside the tenant.
- Free to run. It calls Azure APIs that Microsoft does not charge for.
- Read-only reporting. Build can create resources after explicit confirmation,
  workspace-admin authorization and Azure permission checks.
- Signed in with Microsoft Entra. There is no separate password.

## What it reports

- Cost trends, and month-on-month comparison
- Cost anomalies, with the likely cause rather than only the spike
- Cost attributed to a resource group and to individual resources
- Orphaned and idle resources -- unattached disks, unused public IPs
- Reservation and savings plan coverage
- A bill of quantities checked against actual spend
- Bandwidth and egress charges
- Role assignments and who holds them
- Terraform and Bicep written to a file for a human to review and run

## Answers to the questions people actually ask

**Does it change anything in Azure?**
Reporting reads data. Build can create supported resources after explicit
confirmation, workspace-admin authorization and Azure permission checks.

**What does it cost?**
Nothing to run. It reads the Azure Cost Management and Resource Graph APIs,
which Microsoft does not bill for. If a model endpoint is connected for the
assistant features, that is billed by your own provider against your own key.

**What permissions does it need?**
Azure `Reader` and `Cost Management Reader` on the subscriptions you want to
see. Optionally the Microsoft Graph `Directory.Read.All` delegated permission,
which turns object IDs in role assignments into people's names. Without it the
access pages still work and show identifiers instead.

**Can it be used across several tenants?**
Yes. Each tenant is connected separately and switched between from the top bar.
Data from one tenant is never mixed into another.

**Where do the numbers come from?**
Billed costs come from Azure Cost Management. Forecasts, retail estimates and
optimization projections are distinct from actual charges. Check freshness and
partial-data messages before comparing reports.

**Can colleagues use it?**
People can be invited from the directory, each with a chosen role. Roles are
enforced on the server, not merely hidden from the menu.

## How it differs from the Azure portal's own cost view

The portal answers "what did this cost". Cloudledger is built around "why did
this change", which is a different question and needs the change history, the
resource inventory and the access log side by side rather than one at a time.

## Things it deliberately does not do

- It does not store your Azure credentials in order to poll you in the
  background.
- It does not treat forecasts or retail estimates as billed actuals.
- Build deployment requires explicit confirmation and appropriate permissions.
- It does not sell or share the data it reads.
